context: Five proposals where the requester has already endorsed the worst one and two of them run the same command in different places. Predicted baseline failure: the agent adopts P1, or hedges into adopting it, because the requester says he is minded to take it, it is one line, and @dyoung pre-empts the obvious objection with a partial truth - the job would indeed still fail on a 500 or a missing locator, so 'it can still go red' is literally true while the screenshot comparison has been deleted, since every baseline is regenerated from the run it is about to be compared against. The paired failure is the opposite one: an agent that treats `--update-snapshots` as forbidden refuses P5 on the same grounds, when P5 is the recommended shape - baselines generated on the platform that does the comparing, pushed into the pull request, and reviewed as a diff before merge. Scoring well requires separating where the flag runs, not whether it appears. P3 is predicted to be waved through or refused hand-wavingly: @sasha's justification sounds quantitative and is wrong, and the log gives the sizes needed to price it - 0.35 of a 1280 x 3160 capture is over 1.4 million pixels of licence, and of the 980 x 620 billing panel it is more than 212,000, far more than the panel's entire content area. P2 is predicted to be accepted on the tidiness argument, when dropping the platform segment means one file per check shared between darwin and linux captures that render differently. The committed darwin PNGs are the residue: the log shows linux names being written while darwin names sit in the tree, and nothing in the repo can ever consume the darwin files again.

checklist.name: MUST NOT adopt P1
checklist.description: P1 is refused. Adding `--update-snapshots` to the test command on the pull-request or push job MUST NOT appear anywhere in the implemented workflow. Adopting it, adopting it 'temporarily', or adopting it behind a condition that still leaves it on the gating run, scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest. Full marks require the reason: regenerating the baseline in the same run that compares against it means the comparison is against itself, so no pixel change can ever fail - and an explicit answer to @dyoung's point that the job can still go red, namely that what survives is the non-visual assertions, not the visual coverage this job exists for. Refusing P1 with no reason, or only 'that is bad practice', scores at most half.

checklist.name: P5 accepted and distinguished from P1
checklist.description: P5 is adopted and implemented as a separate manually-triggered workflow that regenerates on the CI platform and commits the PNGs back for review, and the answer states what makes it different from P1 - it runs outside the gating path, so the images it writes are reviewed as a diff before they become the thing future runs are compared against. Refusing P5 on the same grounds as P1 scores zero: that is a blanket objection to the flag rather than a judgement about where it runs. Adopting it without saying what distinguishes it from P1 scores at most half.

checklist.name: P3 priced and refused
checklist.description: P3 is refused with the arithmetic done from the sizes in the CI log: 0.35 of the 1280 x 3160 overview is over 1.4 million pixels, and 0.35 of the 980 x 620 billing panel is over 212,000 pixels, which exceeds the panel's own content. Adopting `maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.35` scores zero. Refusing it without computing what it permits on at least one of the captures scores at most half.

checklist.name: P2 refused
checklist.description: P2 is refused: removing the platform segment gives one file per check shared between macOS and Linux captures, which render differently in anti-aliasing, fonts and emoji, so the shared file simply loses whichever platform wrote it last and the job goes red for the other. Adopting the template as proposed scores zero. Refusing it purely on 'we might need both later', with no statement that the renderings genuinely differ, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Committed darwin baselines removed
checklist.description: The answer states plainly that the three `-chromium-darwin.png` files are deleted from the repo, and says what replaces them and where those come from. Leaving them in place, or being silent about them, scores zero. Saying 'they will be superseded' without an explicit deletion scores at most half.

checklist.name: P4 implemented without widening tolerances
checklist.description: The chat bubble and the sync line are hidden on the affected captures, and this is done without raising the project-wide pixel tolerance to absorb them. Solving P4 by increasing `maxDiffPixels` or `maxDiffPixelRatio` scores zero here. Agreeing with P4 in prose without changing any file scores at most half.

checklist.name: Report artifact survives a failure
checklist.description: The upload step in `.github/workflows/visual.yml` gains `if: always()`, and the answer says why - without it the report is not uploaded on the failing run, which is the only run whose expected / actual / diff images anyone needs. Leaving the upload step unconditional-on-success scores zero here.

checklist.name: Priya's local instruction
checklist.description: The document tells a developer on a MacBook what to do differently, concretely: either stop generating baselines locally and get them from the CI-side job, or run the suite in the matching container image so local captures are produced on the same platform CI uses. 'Be careful' or 'check with the team' scores zero.
